meta.title: Implementation plan: work packages

meta.size_note: Days of focused engineering for one senior engineer, mid-point of a range. Use for relative comparison and critical-path analysis only.

phases.name: Foundations and spikes
phases.goal: Fix the repository structure and test harness, and answer the open technical questions before building on them.
exit: Multi-module build with enforced runtime/control boundary is green in CI
Acceptance-test harness marks test status automatically
Spikes A to E are closed with an ADR each; remaining unknowns have an owner and a validation point
Acceptance status reporting includes Maven Failsafe reports for process-level integration tests
Standalone spike tests have reproducible commands and an explicit CI or manual verification policy

phases.name: Secure governed execution core
phases.goal: A process that runs durably, authenticates people and agents, enforces policy outside the agent, involves humans, and survives failure with explicit idempotency and recovery semantics for business effects.
exit: One end-to-end governed case runs, survives kill -9 and completes once
Traces show workflow, agent, tool and model spans under one correlation id

phases.name: Agent capability
phases.goal: Agents plan and re-plan, use tools and knowledge, remember within scope, collaborate with other agents and with people, all inside the bounds from phase 1.
exit: An unstructured request is resolved by a supervisor agent with two specialists, one over A2A
Limits stop a runaway agent; injected attacks are rejected

phases.name: Governed lifecycle and authority
phases.goal: Everything that changes agent behavior is inventoried, versioned, approved and reversible; in-flight work is pinned; emergency control works without the admin service.
exit: Runtime keeps working with the control application stopped
Revoking a tool or model stops active and waiting tasks within the agreed bound

phases.name: Operations and deployment
phases.goal: The platform can be backed up, upgraded, deployed on several environments, isolated per tenant and scaled with evidence.
exit: T18, T20, T21, T24 pass
Restore and rolling-upgrade drills are automated in CI or a scheduled job
Published RTO and RPO measured, not assumed

phases.name: Quality and model governance
phases.goal: Quality is measured before release and in production; models are chosen by configuration and evaluated consistently.
exit: T10, T31, T38, T39 pass
A quality drop raises an alert and opens a gate review
The same task runs on two providers and a self-hosted model

phases.name: Lifecycle tooling, coexistence and console
phases.goal: Authors, operators and approvers get tooling; legacy coexistence and the governance assistant are delivered.
exit: T27, T29, T33 pass
Operators use the console for all routine tasks; every action is API-backed and audited
All 39 acceptance tests are automated

M01.summary: Validated task contracts, OWS inputs/references and structured outputs; T01 automated.

M02.summary: Bounded contract fields, forbidden actions and escalation authorization; continuous budget enforcement remains open.

M03.summary: PostgreSQL workflow/graph state, restart reconciliation and absolute wait-deadline support exist; effects and multi-node proof remain open.

M04.summary: Idempotent API start and lifecycle recovery exist; event/timer/expiry coverage remains incomplete.

M06.summary: Transactional outbox and idempotent lifecycle requests exist; business-effect ledger, inbox and compensation remain open.

M07.summary: Policy timeout/bulkhead and explicit engine retry settings exist; general dependency/overload guarantees remain open.

M09.summary: Workflow definition identity/version is pinned in lifecycle records; complete artifact pinning and rolling-version proof remain open.

M11.summary: Delegation, JWT verification, token exchange, replay checks, secrets and wait reauthorization exist; T07 uses fakes and the real Keycloak closure gate remains open.

M12.summary: Cedar PEP/PDP, attributable decisions, safe denial/recovery and bounded policy calls exist; non-bypass wiring and production snapshot freshness remain open.

M13.summary: Audit redaction/reference retention and secure secret-file handling exist; platform-wide encryption, erasure and processing-location controls remain open.

M14.summary: Malformed output, forbidden actions and unauthorized escalation are rejected by T01; retrieval/tool defense and optional sandboxing remain open.

M15.summary: Durable hash-chained audit, retention, stamps and query APIs exist; all future decision/effect producers and production access still require integration.

M16.summary: Operator lifecycle APIs, correlation IDs, health and metrics exist; correlated distributed tracing remains open.

M19.summary: PostgreSQL graph checkpoints exist; governed memory, full isolation, retention and growth controls remain open.

M22.summary: Java/Quarkus/PostgreSQL and a configurable model endpoint form a self-hostable foundation; OCI/cluster and offline profiles remain unproved.

M24.summary: Verified tenant context, tenant-scoped grants and lifecycle ownership filters exist; multi-tenant RLS, memory/state/telemetry isolation and the complete isolation suite remain open.

M25.summary: Version-controlled workflow/contract artifacts and build/load validation exist; reusable authoring, packaging and governed promotion remain open.

M26.summary: Execution/control code and dependency boundaries are enforced; production author/approver/runtime privilege separation remains open.

M27.summary: Execution has no control-module dependency and narrow recovery survives policy ERROR; approved-state freshness and administration-outage tests remain open.

M28.summary: Canonical lifecycle registry, task state, outbox projection and reconciler exist; complete effect-aware recovery/T16 remain open.

M29.summary: A fixed plan/draft/review sample graph exists; governed adaptive planning and re-planning remain open.

M34.summary: One sample model endpoint/name is configurable; approved per-task routing, fallback and evaluation remain open.

H01.summary: OWS definitions and schema/reference validation exist; conformance and round-trip loss are not measured.

H02.summary: Framework-free contracts and narrow model/workflow boundaries exist; full adapter/artifact portability remains open.

H12.summary: Acceptance fixtures, fault injection, validation and CI checks exist; authoring/package/promotion UX remains open.

H23.summary: Dependency/licence policy and permissive-source checks run in CI; full supply-chain/SBOM evidence remains open.

H24.summary: Applications/libraries are grouped, contracts remain framework-free and boundaries are checked; broader maintainability is reviewed as features land.

decisions.title: Identity provider
decisions.decision: Keycloak for authentication; delegated authority requires strict actor-bearing token exchange and real-Java evidence. Native Keycloak delegation remains an explicit preview test profile, not a production acceptance claim.

decisions.title: Policy engine
decisions.decision: Cedar embedded; OPA sidecar remains an organizational alternative (ADR 0021).

decisions.title: Target platform
decisions.decision: Recommended: OpenShift and plain Kubernetes, packaged with Helm.

decisions.title: Console technology
decisions.decision: Recommended: Qute unless the console needs a TypeScript SPA.

decisions.title: Model access
decisions.decision: Current implementation: Quarkus LangChain4j through LlmClient. Confirm governed bindings and optional external gateway for WP-503.

decisions.title: Tenancy
decisions.decision: Recommended: single tenant first; introduce row-level security when multi-tenancy is enabled.

decisions.title: AI incident reporting
decisions.decision: Recommended: reporting hook; content and obligations follow the activated deployment profile.

decisions.title: Quarkus 4 and LangChain4j 2
decisions.decision: Stay on the current stable lines; revisit only when final releases are evaluated (issue #26).

decisions.title: Secret store
decisions.decision: Mounted Kubernetes Secrets for static values. Vault where already operated; validate the BOM-pinned 4.9.0 binding before selecting that path.
